prompt:
Native4K 16:9 quiet animation prop identity sheet on a plain light warm-gray background. Two slender yellow-gray bamboo curtain poles, one long and one shorter, horizontal and parallel with ample margin at BOTH complete flat ends. Thin bamboo nodes, no sharp tips, no metal. The poles are dry ordinary theatre supports, with clean bare hand-grip sections at both ends. This is a shape example of a long and a short pole, not the entire inventory of a stage.
On the RIGHT end of the long pole only: ONE thin brown cotton tie makes precisely ONE turn around the bamboo, closed by ONE slipped half-hitch with a small visible doubled pull-loop and short free tail. The loop can be pulled out to release the knot; no knot is inside the solid bamboo, no rope threading through bamboo. No second or third coil. The short pole has no separate knot design. Do not draw a spiral lashing, multiple parallel wraps, a bow with two large loops, or long hanging tails.
Use the upper two-thirds of the canvas for the complete two poles. In the lower-right quarter show just ONE enlarged view of that same right-end binding with exactly the same single-turn/slipped-loop path. All of the enlarged rope must be visible. No other detail views. Keep the lashing brown and thin, and keep the bamboo cylindrical with a flat cut end. Subtle two-level broad shading, fine clean contours and flat low-saturation colors; no texture noise, paper grain, captions, letters, labels, arrows, measurement lines, people, weapons or an assembled theatre.
